summary: SessionBoard's AI Agenda area is an organizer-facing agenda/schedule builder with an embedded "AI Agenda Management Assistant." Organizers build multi-track, multi-day programs by placing sessions into time slots across rooms and tracks (calendar-style drag-and-drop implied). The AI layer continuously monitors the agenda and flags conflicts: speaker double-bookings across time slots, room capacity/booking overlaps, track sequencing issues, and content dependency conflicts, and it suggests resolutions (alternative slots, room swaps, speaker substitutions). A "Scheduler Agent" auto-packs sessions into rooms and tracks from configured constraints, generating a conflict-free draft schedule. Organizers define rule-based agenda logic (session sequencing, speaker constraints, track balancing), get real-time recommendations while editing, run speaker availability checks before moving sessions, and gate changes behind audit/approval flows. The agenda is connected to the speaker database, submission records, and content management, and publishes to the event website. Marketing claims 83% faster agenda launch. The eval focus is the basics: agenda grid with tracks/rooms/slots, conflict detection, and auto-scheduling.
personas: Event organizer / admin (primary: builds and maintains agenda, runs AI scheduler, approves changes)
Speaker (availability and double-booking constraints are checked against them; receives update notifications)
Attendee (consumes published agenda on event website; out of scope for this area's rubric)

user_journeys.name: Manually build a multi-track agenda
steps: Configure event days, time slots, rooms, and tracks
See accepted/unscheduled sessions in a pool or sidebar
Drag (or click-assign) sessions onto specific day/time/room slots
Tag each session with a track; edit session metadata inline
Observe real-time conflict badges appear/disappear as sessions move
user_journeys.filled_state: A 2-day calendar grid with rooms as columns and 30-60 min time slots as rows; 12+ sessions placed, color-coded by 3 tracks; a small pool of unscheduled sessions remaining; one visible conflict badge on a double-booked speaker.

user_journeys.name: AI auto-schedule then review conflicts
steps: With sessions accepted but unscheduled, trigger the AI auto-schedule (Scheduler Agent)
AI packs sessions into rooms/tracks/slots per constraints (speaker availability, track balancing, sequencing rules)
Any residual conflicts are flagged with resolution options (alternative slot, room swap)
Accept or reject suggested resolutions; approve schedule to go live
user_journeys.filled_state: A fully populated grid produced in one action, zero or few conflict flags, a review panel listing AI placement decisions and any flagged conflicts with one-click resolution suggestions.

user_journeys.name: Handle a last-minute change
steps: A speaker cancels or a room becomes unavailable mid-event-prep
Drag the affected session to a new slot/room
System instantly checks speaker availability and flags any new overlaps or broken dependencies
System suggests alternative slots or speaker substitutions
Change passes through approval flow before the public agenda updates
user_journeys.filled_state: Grid mid-edit with one session highlighted, a warning panel showing 'speaker unavailable at this time' plus 2-3 suggested alternative slots, and a pending-approval indicator on the change.

features.name: Agenda builder grid
features.description: Calendar-style agenda builder for multi-track, multi-day programs; organizers place sessions into time slots across rooms/tracks, drag-and-drop with inline session metadata editing (inferred from 'agenda builder' + category norms).
features.ui_expectations: Schedule/timeline view: time axis, rooms or tracks as columns, day switcher/tabs, session cards placed in slots, a pool/sidebar of unscheduled sessions, drag-drop or click-to-assign placement.

features.name: Tracks, rooms, and time slot configuration
features.description: Organizers define event days, time slots, rooms, and tracks that structure the agenda; sessions are assigned a track and a room+slot (setup UI inferred; entities explicitly named throughout copy).
features.ui_expectations: Settings or inline controls to add/edit rooms (with capacity), tracks (with name/color), days and slot durations; new rooms/tracks immediately appear in the grid.

features.name: Automatic conflict detection
features.description: AI continuously monitors the agenda and flags speaker double-bookings across time slots, room capacity/booking overlaps, track sequencing issues, and content dependency conflicts as the agenda is built or edited.
features.ui_expectations: Visible conflict indicators (badge/highlight on session cards, warning toast, or conflicts panel) that appear immediately when a conflicting placement is made and clear when resolved.

features.name: AI auto-scheduling (Scheduler Agent)
features.description: A Scheduler Agent 'packs sessions into rooms and tracks without conflicts' — generates a conflict-free schedule from configured constraints in one action; double-bookings flagged, resolutions suggested.
features.ui_expectations: An 'Auto-schedule' / AI assistant trigger in the agenda builder; after running, unscheduled sessions are placed into slots/rooms; residual conflicts surfaced for human decision.

features.name: Conflict resolution suggestions
features.description: When conflicts are flagged, the system presents actionable resolution options: alternative time slots, room swaps, speaker substitutions; organizer applies with a click.
features.ui_expectations: Conflict detail panel/popover listing 1+ concrete suggested fixes, each applicable directly from the suggestion.

features.name: Rule-based agenda logic
features.description: Organizers create rules that shape the program: session sequencing (dependencies/ordering), speaker constraints (availability windows), track balancing; rules are enforced or violations warned during scheduling.
features.ui_expectations: A rules/constraints UI (per-session dependency field, per-speaker availability, or a rules list); violating a rule during placement produces a visible warning.

features.name: Speaker availability checks
features.description: Before/when moving a session, instantly see if the change impacts a speaker's ability to present or attend other sessions.
features.ui_expectations: Warning when a session is moved to a time its speaker is unavailable or already booked; availability stored on the speaker record (inferred).

features.name: Audit and approval flows
features.description: Agenda changes pass through review/approval so nothing goes live without oversight; change history auditable (mechanics inferred — draft vs. published states are the category norm).
features.ui_expectations: Draft/pending state on edits, an approve/publish action, and a change log or audit trail view.

features.name: Real-time recommendations
features.description: AI suggests schedule updates in real time as the organizer edits, embedded inside the agenda builder rather than a separate tool.
features.ui_expectations: Suggestions appear contextually during editing (inline hints, assistant panel) without page reloads or switching tools.

rubric.criterion: An agenda/schedule builder view exists showing time slots against rooms and/or tracks for a multi-day event, and an unscheduled session can be placed into a specific day/time/room slot.
auto_steps: Log in as organizer and open the event
Navigate to the Agenda/Schedule builder
Confirm a grid/timeline with a time axis, room or track columns, and a day switcher
Locate an unscheduled session (pool/sidebar) and place it into an empty slot via drag-drop or click-assign
Confirm the session card now renders in that slot with its title and time
rubric.pass_criteria: Grid renders with time slots and rooms/tracks; the placement persists in the grid (survives a page reload if checkable).
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of the agenda grid before and after placing the session.

rubric.criterion: Rooms and tracks are configurable by the organizer, and a newly added room/track becomes usable in the agenda grid.
auto_steps: From agenda or event settings, add a new room (e.g., 'Room B', capacity 100)
Add a new track (e.g., 'AI Engineering')
Return to the agenda builder and verify the new room appears as a schedulable column/location
Assign the new track to a session and verify the track shows on the session card or filter
rubric.pass_criteria: Both entities can be created and both are immediately usable for scheduling/tagging sessions.
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of room/track creation forms and of the grid showing the new room column and track label.

rubric.criterion: Scheduling the same speaker in two overlapping sessions produces a visible conflict warning (speaker double-booking detection).
auto_steps: Ensure speaker X is assigned to sessions A and B
Place session A at Day 1 10:00 in Room A
Place session B at Day 1 10:00 in Room B
Observe the UI for a conflict badge, highlight, warning dialog, or conflicts panel entry naming the double-booked speaker or the clashing sessions
rubric.pass_criteria: A conflict indicator appears without manual refresh (or on save) and identifies the overlap; moving session B to a free slot clears it.
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of the conflict indicator while both sessions overlap, and after moving one (indicator gone).

rubric.criterion: Placing two sessions in the same room at overlapping times is flagged or prevented (room double-booking detection).
auto_steps: Place session C at Day 1 11:00 in Room A
Attempt to place session D at Day 1 11:00 in Room A
Observe whether the drop is blocked, or a room-conflict warning/badge appears
rubric.pass_criteria: The overlap is either prevented at placement time or visibly flagged as a room conflict.
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of the blocked placement or the room-conflict warning.

rubric.criterion: An AI auto-schedule action exists that places unscheduled sessions into rooms/tracks/time slots in one operation, yielding a schedule with no flagged conflicts.
auto_steps: Reset to a state with 5+ accepted but unscheduled sessions
Find and trigger the auto-schedule / AI scheduler control in the agenda builder
Wait for completion and verify the previously unscheduled sessions now occupy slots/rooms
Verify no conflict indicators are shown on the generated schedule (including the shared-speaker pair not overlapping)
rubric.pass_criteria: One action schedules the pool; result shows zero conflict flags. Unverified by agent: whether placements genuinely optimize/respect all soft constraints (track balancing, audience needs) — spot-check manually that the known constraints (speaker availability windows, dependency ordering) were honored.
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of the grid before (empty/partial) and after auto-schedule (populated, no conflict badges).

rubric.criterion: When a conflict is flagged, the system offers at least one concrete resolution suggestion (alternative time slot, room swap, or speaker substitution) that can be applied from the UI.
auto_steps: Create a speaker double-booking (as in AIA-03)
Open the conflict indicator/panel
Verify a suggested fix is listed (e.g., 'move to 14:00' or 'swap to Room C')
Apply the suggestion and verify the conflict clears and the session moved as described
rubric.pass_criteria: A specific, applicable suggestion is presented and applying it resolves the conflict.
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of the suggestion UI and of the resolved grid afterward.

rubric.criterion: A scheduling rule/constraint can be defined (speaker availability window or session dependency/ordering) and violating it during manual placement produces a warning.
auto_steps: Set speaker Y as unavailable on Day 2 (or set 'Workshop Part 2 must follow Part 1')
Place speaker Y's session on Day 2 (or place Part 2 before Part 1)
Observe for a rule-violation warning
Move the session to a compliant slot and confirm the warning clears
rubric.pass_criteria: The constraint is definable in the UI and its violation is flagged; compliant placement is clean.
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of the rule definition UI and of the violation warning.

rubric.criterion: Conflict state updates in real time during editing: moving a conflicting session to a free slot clears its indicator immediately, without a full page reload.
auto_steps: With an active conflict from AIA-03 visible, drag one conflicting session to a free slot
Without reloading, verify the conflict indicator disappears within a few seconds
Drag it back and verify the indicator reappears
rubric.pass_criteria: Conflict indicators react live to edits in both directions.
rubric.evidence: Screenshots (or short capture) showing indicator present, then gone after the move, then back.

sample_data: 2-day conference (Day 1–2, 09:00–17:00, 30 and 45 min slots plus a 60-min keynote slot). Rooms: Main Hall (cap 500), Room A (cap 120), Room B (cap 80), Workshop Lab (cap 40). Tracks: AI Engineering, DevTools, Leadership (distinct colors). ~14 accepted sessions with titles/abstracts/durations, 10 speakers. Fixture traps for the rubric: (1) speaker 'Dana Kim' assigned to two different sessions — used to trigger speaker double-booking; (2) speaker 'Raj Patel' available Day 1 only — used for availability-rule violation; (3) 'Hands-on RAG Workshop Part 1' and 'Part 2' with an ordering dependency; (4) one high-demand session (expected attendance 300) to exercise room-capacity conflict if placed in Room B; (5) 5+ sessions left unscheduled to feed the auto-schedule test.
gaps: Marketing pages contain no actual product screenshots or alt-text describing the builder UI, so the concrete layout (grid orientation, unscheduled-session sidebar, conflict badge styling, auto-schedule button placement) is inferred from category norms (Sessionize/Cvent/Grip-style agenda builders). Not learnable from sources: how speaker availability is captured (speaker-entered vs organizer-entered), the exact rules-engine UI, approval-flow mechanics (draft vs published states inferred), whether auto-scheduling is one-click batch vs conversational AI assistant, room capacity conflict thresholds, and any attendee-facing published-agenda behavior. Three of the page's benefit sections repeated identical bullet text, suggesting thin/templated copy — treated as low-signal. The 83% agenda-launch-time claim is a case-study metric, not a testable feature.
